item.title: Chancellor Merz backs Ilse Aigner as Germany's first female President
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has endorsed Ilse Aigner for the upcoming presidential election in Germany. Aigner, if elected, would be the first woman to hold this position. Supported by the Christian Democratic Union and the Christian Social Union, she has backing from various political parties. She could succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose presidency ends on March 18. Aigner has previous government experience and a strong political network in Germany.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: ‘Task Force Iron Gate in full force' to choke Iran's trade route, says Trump
item.description: Task Force Iron Gate is a new US initiative aimed at disrupting Iran's overland supply routes and preventing advanced weapons movement. It involves around 20 personnel coordinating with various US agencies from Tampa, Florida. The task force complements an existing naval blockade that has already hindered Iran's oil exports significantly. Humanitarian aid will remain exempt from these restrictions despite the new measures.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 'Immigration policy too tough': 5 key takeaways from Trump's 60 minutes interview
item.description: Donald Trump admitted in a recent interview that the Iran war and deportation policies affected Republican midterm results. He acknowledged that while strong border security was supported, harsh deportation measures raised concerns among voters. Trump expressed a willingness to negotiate with Democrats on immigration reform, particularly for long-term residents. He maintained that Iran was prevented from obtaining nuclear weapons during his presidency, asserting military involvement in the region.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Peat from ancient forests off Mozambique dates back up to about 5,000 years
item.description: Submerged ancient peat forests off Mozambique's coast have transformed into vibrant marine ecosystems, offering vital habitats for diverse marine life. As rising sea levels allowed these forests to sink, they have now integrated with coral reefs, enhancing local biodiversity. The carbon-rich legacy of these underwater realms also holds significant implications for climate strategies, highlighting the necessity of including peat reefs in conservation initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: South Carolina permanently protected more than 62,000 acres of working forest
item.description: South Carolina has successfully protected over 62,000 acres of forestland with the Pee Dee Basin Initiative. This initiative represents a significant collaboration among various government and private organizations, totaling an investment of $70 million. The protected areas will support sustainable timber production while preventing incompatible development that undermines ecological integrity. In addition, this initiative will enhance local wildlife habitats and strengthen natural flood defenses for surrounding communities.

item.title: Baby pufferfish inherit a nearly non-toxic chemical from their mothers
item.description: In a fascinating discovery, researchers have found that mother pufferfish provide their larvae with a nearly non-toxic chemical that effectively helps them escape predators. This chemical deters potential threats by making them unpalatable, thus improving the young fish's chances of survival. Additionally, this same chemical intriguingly attracts other pufferfish, revealing a unique dual role that aids in their survival strategies during vulnerable stages.

item.title: Stanford scientists have built a fingernail-sized chip that turns jumbled light into clean beams
item.description: Stanford University researchers have developed a groundbreaking chip that effectively segregates mixed light into its individual components. This novel technology facilitates the analysis of coherence modes of light that were once challenging to identify. Utilizing advanced photonic techniques, the chip can enhance applications in fields like imaging and astronomy, potentially transforming our understanding of microscopic particles and faraway celestial phenomena.

item.title: 16-year-old builds free wildfire warning checker, teaches California seniors to use it after brush fire
item.description: Vedant Thakker created the Red Flag Check application to evaluate wildfire risks utilizing data from the National Weather Service. This innovative tool classifies residential locations under red flag warnings into four specific risk categories, empowering local residents. It is specially designed for older adults who may face increased vulnerability during wildfires.

item.title: Firehouse Townhouse Sells: Former Manhattan station fetches $19m; includes underground jazz club
item.description: A historic fire station in Manhattan has been transformed into a luxury townhouse and sold for $19 million. It originally served the community as a firehouse for over a century before being decommissioned. The property underwent extensive renovations, highlighting its unique features such as an underground jazz club. Notably, the townhouse retains elements of its industrial past while incorporating modern living spaces.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Historic Brooklyn mansion returns to market for $20.99M
item.description: Once a forgotten gem, a historic mansion in Brooklyn Heights from 1852 has been meticulously transformed and is now available for $14.99 million. The adjacent carriage house can be purchased separately for $6 million. After a decade-long renovation focused on preserving its original beauty while integrating luxury amenities, this estate invites potential buyers to explore various living arrangements, from family homes to vibrant workspaces.

item.title: How two Wisconsin students built a volunteer network to fight hunger
item.description: In Middleton, Wisconsin, Noah Duckett and Wyatt Ehrhardt launched a food drive aimed at tackling food insecurity. This initiative blossomed into Meals Matter, a national non-profit featuring over 35 student-led chapters. With more than $550,000 raised and countless young volunteers participating nationwide, both founders were honored with The Diana Award, showcasing how youth can lead transformative social change.

item.title: Rotten Roots: family turns yard into walk-through Halloween haunt; visitors trigger effects
item.description: In Pennsylvania, a family has dedicated five years to crafting an enchanting Halloween experience known as Rotten Roots. This immersive yard display combines a thrilling storyline of witches and alien invaders with interactive decorations, enhanced through a special app. As they continue to expand their attraction with new characters and mechanics, the family fosters deeper bonds within the local Halloween enthusiast community.
